value.description: The new value of the member. Left out, the member keeps the value it has stored.

previousName.description: The name the member had before this update, when the update renames it; its stored value moves with it.

BoxRetention.description: What happens to a session's box after each of its turns, whatever the turn's outcome. A snapshot follows every turn in each mode.

BuildProvider.description: A build provider that runs prebuilds on the tenant's own account and bills it.

Channel.BaseImageDownload.description:
The base image of a layered boot, the current release's ReleaseBaseImage for the host's
architecture. `imageUrl`, `kernelUrl` and `manifestUrl` are presigned GETs of the ext4 image, the
kernel and the BaseImageManifest document stored under `imageDigest`, `kernelDigest` and
`manifestDigest` in the release bucket.

Channel.BootImage.description: What a box boots from: a full guest image, or a base image with a harness layer.

Channel.BoxDiscard.description:
Asks the host to drop a box of a session that moved to another host, even when the box holds a
completed turn no snapshot holds, or of a session whose repository the box could not clone. The host answers BoxGone, also when it runs no such box.

Channel.BoxGone.description: The host runs no box of the session any more and returned its TAP device to the pool.

Channel.BoxTeardownFailed.description: The host kept the box. `detail` states what failed and what fixes it.

Channel.BoxTeardownFailureReason.description: Why the host kept a box it was asked to tear down.

Channel.ChunkPlacement.description:
Where one chunk is stored: the chunk whose bytes have the lower-case hex SHA-256 `digest` lies
`length` bytes long at byte `offset` of the pack `packDigest`. A pack is chunks concatenated, about
8 MiB of them, stored under `<tenantId>/packs/<packDigest>`, where `packDigest` is the SHA-256 of
the whole pack.

Channel.ClaudeSetupBoxCode.description:
The code the person submitted, for the standard input of the setup's `claude setup-token`; the
host forwards it to the box once and keeps no copy. The box fails the setup MintTimedOut when
Claude Code prints no token within `mintBudgetSeconds` of the code.

Channel.ClaudeSetupBoxDiscard.description:
Asks the host to stop the setup's box and delete its drive, also in place of an unacked offer or
code of a setup that ended. The host answers nothing, and does nothing when it runs no such box.

Channel.ClaudeSetupBoxFailed.description:
The setup's box stopped without storing the token and is gone. `detail` states what failed and
what fixes it, and never holds the token.

Channel.ClaudeSetupBoxOffer.description:
Asks the host to boot box `boxId` from `image` with no repository, no persona files and no
credential, and run `claude setup-token` in it for Claude setup `claudeSetupId`. The host answers
ClaudeSetupBoxUrl once the command prints its sign-in URL, hands the code of a ClaudeSetupBoxCode
to the command's standard input, and answers ClaudeSetupBoxFailed when the box stops without
storing the token. `harness` names the harness at `harnessVersion` that `image` boots, and an offer
without it names ClaudeCode. Only the box writes the token: it POSTs it to `tokenUrl` with `tokenCredential`
as its bearer token, and the host never sees it. `tokenCredential` is bound to this setup and
writes its token once, while the setup is Minting. The host stops the box at `expiresAt`, when it stores the token, or on
ClaudeSetupBoxDiscard, and deletes its drive.

Channel.ClaudeSetupBoxUrl.description: The setup's `claude setup-token` printed the URL where the person signs in.

Channel.DispatchConnector.description:
One connector of a turn. `url` is the upstream MCP server. `tokenUrl` is the control plane's
ConnectorTokens_fetch for this turn and connector, and `tokenCredential` its ConnectorTurnToken,
valid while the turn is Running. The guest keeps both in forwarder memory only: never in the
harness environment, a file, a log or a snapshot, and a new tokenCredential never restarts the
harness. `name` is the connector's name; the guest derives each harness's MCP server name from it,
and from `connectorId` when a control plane leaves it out.

arguments.description: The harness arguments the catalog maps the credential to; they hold no secret. A grant without them gives the guest none.

credentialFile.description: A CredentialFile credential: the guest writes `value` to `path` under the harness home, mode 0600, before the harness starts, and deletes it at the end of the turn.

connectors.description: The session's connectors, none when its persona lists none. The guest forwarder serves each at its loopback route and fetches its access token from tokenUrl with tokenCredential. Neither reaches the harness.

Channel.DispatchGrant.description:
The dispatch variables for one offer: every member of the persona's secret set, the credential for
the harness's provider under the variable its kind maps to and every other member under its own
name. The control plane decrypts them from the secret set each time it sends or resends a
TurnOffer, keeps no plaintext copy and records the variable names in an append-only handover log;
`credentialHandoverId` names this handover in the supervisor's errors. `expiresAt`, the end of
the turn's credential span (the longer of dispatchGrantTtlSeconds and turnOfferTtlSeconds plus
turnImageFetchBudgetSeconds, from when the offer was sent), is when the supervisor stops handing
the variables to a box and fails the turn DispatchCredentialExpired instead.

Channel.DispatchVariable.description: One environment variable for one turn: a secret set member's value. It lives in box memory only and is never written to the host's disk.

Channel.GuestImageDownload.description:
The full guest image of the turn, from the current ReleaseManifest, for the session's harness version
and the architecture the host enrolled with, offered while the release lacks a base image or a
harness layer for them. `imageUrl`, `kernelUrl` and `manifestUrl` are presigned
GETs of the ext4 image, the kernel and the GuestImageManifest document stored under
`imageDigest`, `kernelDigest` and `manifestDigest` in the release bucket, valid until
`downloadExpiresAt`, turnOfferTtlSeconds plus `fetchSeconds` after the send of the offer. A supervisor whose
image cache lacks `imageDigest` sends TurnImageFetching and downloads the three within `fetchSeconds` of
sending it, counting the wait for another image the host is fetching; it fetches one image at a time,
checks each against its digest and only then moves them into the cache, replacing the cached image
of the same harness version; it skips the kernel when the cache holds `kernelDigest`. A download
that fails, misses its digest or names another image in its manifest fails the turn ImageFetchFailed,
one that outlasts `fetchSeconds` fails it ImageFetchTimedOut.

Channel.HarnessLayerDownload.description:
The harness layer of a layered boot, the current release's ReleaseHarnessLayer for the session's
harness version and the host's architecture. `layerUrl` and `manifestUrl` are presigned GETs of
the squashfs file and the HarnessLayerManifest document stored under `layer.layerDigest` and
`layer.manifestDigest` in the release bucket.

Channel.LayeredImageDownload.description:
The layered boot of the turn, offered when the current release carries a base image for the
host's architecture and a harness layer for the session's harness version on it. The box boots
from the base, the guest drive of the host's supervisor and the layer. The URLs are valid until
`downloadExpiresAt`, turnOfferTtlSeconds plus `fetchSeconds` after the send of the offer. A supervisor whose
cache lacks the base or the layer sends TurnImageFetching naming the first part it lacks, then
fetches base, kernel and layer within one `fetchSeconds` of sending it, counting the wait for
another fetch on the host, and checks each against its digest before it moves it into the cache. A
download that fails, misses its digest or names another part in its manifest fails the turn
ImageFetchFailed, one that outlasts `fetchSeconds` fails it ImageFetchTimedOut. The host keeps the
base and the layer in its cache while a box runs on them.

Channel.Pack.description: One pack: `packDigest` is the SHA-256 of its `sizeBytes` bytes.

Channel.PackUrl.description:
One pack object stored under `<tenantId>/packs/<packDigest>`, `sizeBytes` long, and `url` a
presigned URL of that object alone.

Channel.PersonaFileDownload.description:
One file of the session's persona. `downloadUrl` is a presigned GET of the blob stored under
`digest`, valid until `downloadExpiresAt`, the DispatchGrant's expiresAt. The supervisor
checks the bytes against `digest` and keeps them in its cache, so a digest it already holds is
not fetched again.

Channel.RestoreChunks.description:
Part `part` of the chunks a box that boots cold needs for turn `turnId` and lacks in the host's
chunk cache, each at the placement its manifest or root names, at most
ChunkExchange.DigestsPerPart of them, grouped by pack. The host sends each next part once the
answer to the one before arrived, and starts the downloads of each part as its answer arrives.
The control plane answers RestoreDownloads.

Channel.RestoreDownloads.description:
The answer to RestoreChunks part `part`: a presigned GET for each pack that holds chunks of that
part, valid until `downloadExpiresAt`, the DispatchGrant's expiresAt. A pack is left out when
any chunk asked in it is no chunk of the session at that placement, and the host fails the turn
SnapshotUnreadable.

Channel.SnapshotChunks.description:
Part `part` of the chunk digests the files of a snapshot hold that the box's previous snapshot
did not, at most ChunkExchange.DigestsPerPart of them. The host sends part 1 once its files are
cut, and each next part once the answer to the one before arrived. The control plane answers
SnapshotChunksHeld and counts each digest as referenced by the session.

Channel.SnapshotChunksHeld.description:
The answer to SnapshotChunks part `part`: where the tenant stores each digest of that part it
holds already. A digest left out is stored in no pack, and the host packs and uploads it.

Channel.SnapshotDone.description: The host stored the snapshot's packs and root. `uploadedBytes` counts the bytes it uploaded: the packs the tenant lacked, plus the root.

Channel.SnapshotDownload.description:
One stored snapshot of a session, for a box that boots cold. `downloadUrl` is a presigned GET of
the SnapshotRoot under `storageKey` alone, valid until `downloadExpiresAt`, the end of the turn's
credential span, the DispatchGrant's expiresAt.

Channel.SnapshotFailed.description: The host could not store the snapshot. `detail` states what failed and what fixes it.

Channel.SnapshotFailureReason.description: Why the host could not store a snapshot.

Channel.SnapshotPacks.description:
Part `part` of the chunks a snapshot packed: where each chunk lies, at most
ChunkExchange.DigestsPerPart of them, and the size of each pack they lie in. A pack whose chunks
run past one part is listed again in the next. The host sends part 1 once its packs are written,
and each next part once the answer to the one before arrived. The control plane keeps the
placements until SnapshotDone, counts each digest as referenced by the session, and answers
SnapshotPackUploads.

Channel.SnapshotPackUploads.description:
The answer to SnapshotPacks part `part`: a presigned PUT for each pack of that part the tenant
holds no object for, valid until `uploadExpiresAt`. Each URL signs the pack's SHA-256 as the
x-amz-checksum-sha256 header, so the host sends that header and object storage refuses bytes that
do not hash to the key. A pack left out is stored already.

Channel.SupervisorUpdateFailed.description:
The host's supervisor update stopped. `detail` states what failed and what fixes it.
`outputTail` holds the last lines the candidate printed in its dry run, token-shaped runs
hidden, and is empty for every other reason.

Channel.SupervisorUpdateStep.description:
The host's supervisor update from the binary `fromSha256` to `toSha256` entered `phase`. The new
binary sends Online once it reaches Welcome after the swap.

Channel.TurnClaim.description:
The host accepts the offered turn. It sends this at once, before it fetches the image, restores the
snapshot or boots the box; those keep their own budgets and failures. The control plane answers TurnClaimed
and the turn reads Running, or answers TurnWithdrawn when the turn already left Offered. The host
hands the prompt to the harness only once TurnClaimed arrived and the box is ready. A host that
gives up waiting for the answer hands nothing and fails the turn NotClaimed, and the control plane
offers the turn again. So a turn is either claimed and its result reaches the control plane, or
refused before the harness starts.

Channel.TurnClaimed.description: The control plane's answer to a TurnClaim for a turn that was still Offered; the turn now reads Running, and the host hands its prompt to the harness once the box is ready.

credentialFile.description: The turn's credential file as the harness rewrote it; the control plane stores it in place of the secret set's CredentialFile member.

warning.description: The guest's warning for a turn the harness completed, such as a box disk with less than a hundredth of it free; the control plane shows it on the turn read.

Channel.TurnComplete.description: The harness finished the turn. `lastLineSeq` is the turn's final line; the control plane holds every line up to it and stores the snapshot after it before the turn reads Completed, and fails the turn SnapshotNotStored when that snapshot is not stored.

credentialFile.description: The turn's credential file as the harness rewrote it; the control plane stores it in place of the secret set's CredentialFile member.

Channel.TurnImageFetching.description:
The host's cache lacks part of the offer's image and the host has started to download it: `imageDigest` names
the full image, or the base image or harness layer of a layered boot, whichever it lacks first.
It follows the TurnClaim; the host fails the turn ImageFetchTimedOut when the fetch outlasts the
offer's `image.fetchSeconds`.

Channel.TurnLine.description: One harness-native JSONL line. `lineSeq` continues the session's line count, so lines of a turn arrive in `lineSeq` order with no gap.

Channel.TurnRepositoryCloneFailed.description: The box could not clone the session's repository; the turn fails RepositoryCloneFailed. `detail` carries what git reported.

Channel.TurnRepositoryReady.description: The box holds the session's repository and the harness is about to get the prompt; the first-line budget starts here.

Channel.TurnWithdrawn.description:
Takes the place of an unacked TurnOffer when the control plane resends it after its turn left
Offered, so the resend keeps every `seq` and no key reaches a turn that already ended. It is also
the answer to a TurnClaim for a turn that left Offered before the claim arrived: the host then
hands the turn no prompt, keeps the box warm and reports nothing for the turn.

CircleCIAuthorization.description:
One OAuth 2.0 authorization code flow with PKCE S256 that connects the tenant's CircleCI
organization. The tenant's own client, registered once through CircleCI's dynamic client
registration, sends the person to CircleCI's consent page; CircleCI sends the browser back to a
loopback address. The verifier and the token are held sealed and never answered.

authorizeUrl.description: CircleCI's consent page, with this authorization's client_id, PKCE S256 challenge and state.

redirectUri.description: The loopback address CircleCI sends the browser to, http://127.0.0.1:47151/circleci/callback; nothing listens there unless the tumpel CLI does.

redirectDueAt.description: When the redirect address must arrive by, or the authorization fails AuthorizationTimedOut.

chooseDueAt.description: When the organization must be chosen by, or the authorization fails AuthorizationTimedOut and the token is discarded.

detail.description: What failed and what fixes it.

CircleCIAuthorizationFailureReason.description: Why a CircleCI authorization ended Failed. Each reason names the phase it stopped in.

CircleCIAuthorizationStatus.description: Where a CircleCI authorization is: the consent URL while it waits for the redirect, the organizations while it waits for a choice, the organization once Completed, the reason once Failed.

apiToken.description: A personal API token of a member of the organization; CircleCI's API v2 refuses project tokens.

CircleCIConnectionStart.description: Connects CircleCI with a pasted token, the fallback to an authorization. The control plane checks the token with GET /api/v2/me and seals it; no operation answers it.

slug.description: The organization's slug, such as gh/acme or circleci/<id>.

CircleCIOrganization.description: A CircleCI organization the authorized token reads, from GET /api/v2/me/collaborations.

repository.description: The repository as https://github.com/<owner>/<name> in lower case.

projectId.description: The CircleCI project id, read from the project at the binding.

pipelineDefinitionId.description: The pipeline definition the prebuilds run, from Project Settings > Project Setup.

CircleCIProject.description:
Binds one repository to the CircleCI project and pipeline definition its prebuilds run. The
pipeline definition must check out the repository.

CircleCIProjectSlug.description:
A CircleCI project slug: gh/<owner>/<name> in a GitHub OAuth organization, or
circleci/<organization id>/<project id> in a GitHub App organization.

CircleCIUuid.description: A CircleCI id: an organization, a project or a pipeline definition, as a lower-case UUID.

ClaudeSetup.description:
A short-lived box that signs in to the setup's harness and stores the token in a secret set: it
runs `claude setup-token` from the tenant's pinned Claude Code and stores the SubscriptionToken
member CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN for Anthropic, or `codex login --device-auth` from the pinned Codex
and stores the auth.json it writes as the CredentialFile member CODEX_AUTH_JSON for OpenAi. The box gets no secret set member and no GitHub token,
and the token never appears in any response.

signInUrl.description: Where the person signs in; for Claude Code the page shows the code to submit.

userCode.description: The one-time code a Codex setup shows, for the person to enter at signInUrl. A Codex setup takes no submitted code: its box stores the token once the person signs in.

codeDueAt.description: When the code must arrive by, or for Codex the sign-in must finish by, or the setup fails SetupTimedOut.

ClaudeSetupAwaitingCode.description: The box printed its sign-in URL and waits for the code the sign-in page shows.

ClaudeSetupCodeText.description: The sign-in code a person pastes after signing in at a Claude setup's signInUrl.

memberName.description: The member the setup wrote: the SubscriptionToken CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN for Anthropic, or the CredentialFile CODEX_AUTH_JSON for OpenAi.

expiresAt.description: When the stored token stops working; for Codex, when the access token in the file does, which Codex refreshes itself.

ClaudeSetupCompleted.description: The secret set holds the minted token.

detail.description: What failed and what fixes it.

ClaudeSetupFailed.description: The setup stopped without storing a token; the secret set is unchanged.

ClaudeSetupFailureReason.description: Why a Claude setup ended Failed. Each reason names the phase it stopped in.

ClaudeSetupHarness.description: The harness a Claude setup signs in to: Claude Code with claude setup-token, or Codex with codex login --device-auth.

ClaudeSetupMember.description: The secret set member a Claude setup writes: the variable its harness reads a subscription token from.

tokenDueAt.description: When the setup fails SetupTimedOut unless the box stored the token or reported why not: claudeSetupMintBudgetSeconds plus claudeSetupMintGraceSeconds after the code.

ClaudeSetupMinting.description: The box has the code and waits for Claude Code to mint and store the token.

urlDueAt.description: When the box must print its sign-in URL by, or the setup fails SetupUrlMissing.

ClaudeSetupStarting.description: The box is booting on its host.

ClaudeSetupStatus.description: Where a Claude setup is, with the facts of its state: the time each live phase ends by, the sign-in URL while it waits for the code, the member once Completed, the reason once Failed. A setup read past the end of its phase reads Failed.

ClaudeSetupUserCode.description: The one-time code Codex prints for the person to enter at the sign-in URL.

boxId.description: The control plane mints the id of the box that runs the turn.

goal.description: A condition the harness keeps working toward until it holds; only a session whose harness has goals in the harness catalog accepts it.

lineCount.description: How many transcript lines this turn has written so far, counting its own lines alone. A line's `lineSeq` numbers the session's lines instead, so the turn's last line is the `lineSeq` the session held before the turn plus `lineCount`.

image.description: The image the turn's box boots, recorded when the control plane offers the turn. A turn not yet offered has none.

warning.description: A condition the turn completed under that the persona should act on, such as a box disk with less than a hundredth of it free, with its size and the boxDiskMib that raises it. Absent when there was none.

Connector.description: A connector of either credential kind.

ConnectorAccessToken.description:
An access token for one connector of one running turn. The forwarder sends it upstream until
fewer than 30 seconds remain before expiresAt, then fetches another. A token without expiresAt is
fetched once.

ConnectorAuth.description: How a connector's upstream credential is held: one static token, or an OAuth grant.

authorizeUrl.description: The provider's authorization page, with the control plane's callback, this authorization's PKCE S256 challenge, its signed state and the resource.

callbackDueAt.description: When the callback must arrive by, or the connector reads AuthorizationFailed AuthorizationExpired.

ConnectorAuthorization.description:
One OAuth authorization of a connector. Open authorizeUrl in a browser; the provider sends the
browser back to the control plane's callback, which stores the grant. Connectors_get reads the
outcome. A newer authorization of the same connector replaces this one.

detail.description: What failed and what fixes it, with the provider's answer sanitized; it never quotes a token response.

ConnectorAuthorizationFailureReason.description: Why an OAuth connector's authorization or refresh failed after authorize answered. Each reason names the phase it stopped in.

ConnectorStatus.description: Whether a connector serves new turns, with when it connected, when it was disconnected, or why its authorization failed.

ConnectorUrl.description:
The HTTPS address of a remote MCP server that speaks Streamable HTTP. It carries no user info, no
query and no fragment, so it never holds a credential.

CostBasis.description:
Whether a turn on a credential reports what it cost and whether that cost is billed. A turn records
its tokens as turn.tokens and, unless NotReported, its cost as turn.cost in micro-US-dollars, both
with the basis as their costBasis dimension.

expiresAt.description: When the access token in the file stops working. Shown only: the harness refreshes the file itself, so a turn is not refused for it.
When the access token in the file stops working. Shown only: the harness refreshes the file itself, so a turn is not refused for it.

value.description: The new value of the member. Left out, the member keeps the value it has stored.

previousName.description: The name the member had before this update, when the update renames it; its stored value moves with it.

expiresAt.description: When the access token in the file stops working. Shown only: the harness refreshes the file itself, so a turn is not refused for it.

repositoryCredentialSource.description: Where the GITHUB_TOKEN this offer carried came from.

CredentialHandover.description:
One offer of a turn's credentials to its box, appended when the control plane sent the turn offer.
`variableNames` lists the variables handed over; values are never recorded or returned.

CredentialKind.description: The kinds of provider credential a secret set can hold.

EventPage.description:
A page of the tenant's events, oldest first, at most 100. `lastEventId` is the id the read
reached; pass it as `afterEventId` to read on.

boxId.description: The control plane mints the id of the box that runs the turn.

goal.description: A condition the harness keeps working toward until it holds; only a session whose harness has goals in the harness catalog accepts it.

lineCount.description: How many transcript lines this turn has written so far, counting its own lines alone. A line's `lineSeq` numbers the session's lines instead, so the turn's last line is the `lineSeq` the session held before the turn plus `lineCount`.

image.description: The image the turn's box boots, recorded when the control plane offers the turn. A turn not yet offered has none.

detail.description: What failed and what fixes it, with the tail of the harness's standard error when there is one.

FailedTurn.description: A turn that ended Failed, with why.

FixedVariable.description: A variable a turn gets with a fixed value beside a credential, such as the base URL of the provider serving the harness's model API.

accountLabel.description: The account GitHub Actions bills, as the tenant names it.

callerWorkflow.description: The caller workflow each repository holds; the start commits or dispatches it and the job token must name it.

GitHubActionsConnection.description:
The tenant's GitHub Actions build provider. A prebuild dispatches the caller workflow in the
repository, which calls Tumpel's reusable prebuild workflow; the job's upload is accepted only
from a run of that workflow.

GitHubIssueNumber.description: The number of an issue in its repository.

Goal.description: A condition the harness keeps working toward until it holds.

path.description: For a CredentialFile, the file under the harness home the guest writes it to, mode 0600, in place of the variable; the harness may rewrite it, and a changed file is stored back in the secret set at the end of the turn.

HarnessCredential.description:
A credential a harness accepts, and what a turn gets from it: the credential under `variable`,
the `fixed` variables beside it, and the `arguments` the guest adds to the harness command, such
as the Codex model provider that reads `variable`. The arguments hold no secret.

HarnessPin.description: The harness version a tenant runs for one harness. It names an entry of the harness catalog.

HarnessPinCreate.description: The harness version a tenant runs for one harness. It names an entry of the harness catalog.

HostLabel.description: A label a host carries for placement, such as gpu or region-eu.

HostUsage.description:
What a host holds at one moment, sent on Hello and on every host Heartbeat. `boxesWarm` counts
the paused boxes it holds, `loadAverage` is the one-minute load average of the host,
and `memoryAvailableMib` is MemAvailable of /proc/meminfo in MiB. `diskBudgetMib` is the disk the
host gives box disks: the free disk under its dataDir and what its boxes already wrote, less the
headroom it keeps free. `diskHeldMib` is the sum of the disk sizes of the boxes it holds. A host
admits a box only while its disk fits the budget beside the held ones; a supervisor older than
the box disk budget sends neither. `memoryBudgetMib` is the memory the host gives boxes: MemTotal
less the headroom it keeps free. `memoryHeldMib` is the sum of the `boxMemoryMib` of the boxes it
holds. A host admits a box only while its memory fits the budget beside the held ones, whatever
their count; a supervisor older than the memory budget sends neither.

ImageHarness.description: The harness of a guest image's GuestHarness: a catalog harness, or Shell for the test image the proof's Shell harness steps boot.

NamespaceWorkspaceId.description: A Namespace workspace id, such as tenant_123456789ab.

OAuthConnector.description:
A remote MCP server the tenant connects once through OAuth. An Owner authorizes it in a browser,
the control plane holds the grant sealed and refreshes it, and every session in the tenant whose
persona lists it reaches it through the box's loopback forwarder. The URL is fixed at create.

boxId.description: The control plane mints the id of the box that runs the turn.

goal.description: A condition the harness keeps working toward until it holds; only a session whose harness has goals in the harness catalog accepts it.

lineCount.description: How many transcript lines this turn has written so far, counting its own lines alone. A line's `lineSeq` numbers the session's lines instead, so the turn's last line is the `lineSeq` the session held before the turn plus `lineCount`.

image.description: The image the turn's box boots, recorded when the control plane offers the turn. A turn not yet offered has none.

OpenRouterAuthorization.description:
One OAuth PKCE S256 flow at OpenRouter that mints an API key and stores it in a secret set as the
ApiKey member OPENROUTER_API_KEY for OpenRouter. OpenRouter sends the browser back to the control
plane, which spends the code with the verifier it holds sealed and then sends the browser to
the secret set's page with openRouterAuthorizationId added. The code, the verifier and the key never appear in
a response.

authorizeUrl.description: OpenRouter's authorization page, with the control plane's callback_url, this authorization's PKCE S256 challenge and its signed state.

callbackDueAt.description: When the callback must arrive by, or the authorization fails AuthorizationTimedOut.

keyLabel.description: The label the key carries on OpenRouter, where its owner deletes it.

exchangeDueAt.description: When the exchange must have stored a key by, or the authorization fails ExchangeFailed.

detail.description: What failed and what fixes it.

OpenRouterAuthorizationFailureReason.description: Why an OpenRouter authorization ended Failed. Each reason names the phase it stopped in.

OpenRouterAuthorizationStatus.description: Where an OpenRouter authorization is: the authorization URL while it waits for the callback, the exchange time limit while it spends the code, the key label once Completed, the reason once Failed.

PersonaFilePath.description: A path relative to the harness home in the box, such as .claude/settings.json. The harness catalog lists the paths each harness accepts.

PersonaFileSize.description: The size of a persona file in bytes, at most PersonaFileLimit.PersonaBytes.

personaId.description: The persona whose secret set's GITHUB_TOKEN read the inputs when the tenant has no GitHub App installation for the repository, whose harness version picks the guest image, and whose name the job's subject carries.

repository.description: The repository as https://github.com/<owner>/<name> in lower case, whatever form the start named it in.

inputDigest.description:
The sha256 over the repository's devcontainer files and lockfiles on its default branch: every
file under .devcontainer/, the file .devcontainer.json, and these lockfiles at the repository
root: package-lock.json, npm-shrinkwrap.json, yarn.lock, pnpm-lock.yaml, bun.lock, bun.lockb,
Cargo.lock, go.sum, uv.lock, poetry.lock, Pipfile.lock, Gemfile.lock, composer.lock, mix.lock,
pubspec.lock and flake.lock, and the manifest the default config reads: package.json. For each
file present, in byte order of its path, one line
`<path>` NUL `<git blob sha of the file>` LF; the digest is the sha256 of those lines.

guestImageDigest.description:
The digest of the guest image the layer is built on: the current release's image of the
persona's harness version for Amd64. A layer is a diff against its image, so a new image needs
a new prebuild. Prebuilds build on Amd64 until the release carries Arm64 images.

provider.description: The provider the start named. The prebuild runs on one of the tenant's online Amd64 hosts, as a turn of a session the session list leaves out.

logUrl.description: The transcript of the prebuild's turn: the output of the repository's setup step.

Prebuild.description:
A repository's dependencies installed once by a build provider on the tenant's account, stored as
one layer. The repository, the input digest and the guest image digest are its key: every commit
with the same devcontainer files and lockfiles, built on the same guest image, shares one
prebuild. A prebuild exists only once its provider accepted the job.

PrebuildConfigSource.description: Where the commands a prebuild runs came from.

layerDigest.description: The sha256 of the compressed OCI layer the job uploaded.
The sha256 of the OCI layer the provider uploaded.

detail.description: What failed, with what the provider reported.

PrebuildFailure.description: Why a prebuild ended Failed. Exists only for a prebuild in state Failed; the prebuild's status holds when.

PrebuildFailurePhase.description: The phase a Failed prebuild stopped in. A provider that refuses the job refuses the start, and no prebuild exists.

PrebuildLayerAbsence.description: Why a session's files start without a prebuild's layer.

PrebuildStatus.description: Where a prebuild is, with the facts of its state: the layer once Done, the failed phase once Failed.

PushEndpointUrl.description: The HTTPS push service address a browser's push subscription names.

PushSubscription.description:
One browser of the caller that receives a Web Push notification for each of the tenant's events
of the listed types. A push service that answers 404 or 410 deletes the
subscription.

PushSubscriptionCreate.description: What a browser sends to subscribe: its push endpoint, its keys and the event types to notify. The keys are write-only.

p256dh.description: The browser's P-256 public key, uncompressed.

PushSubscriptionKeys.description: The keys a browser's push subscription carries, in base64url, as the Push API reports them.

ReleaseHarnessLayer.description:
One harness layer of a release, for one harness version and architecture: a read-only squashfs
image compressed with zstd whose root is `/opt/harness/<harness>/<harnessVersion>` in the box.
The squashfs file and its HarnessLayerManifest document are stored under
`layers/<harness>/<harnessVersion>/<arch>/<digest>` by `layerDigest` and `manifestDigest`.
`sizeBytes` is the size of the squashfs file. A host attaches a layer only once its sha256
matches `layerDigest`.

ReportedHostUsage.description:
A host's box slots and its last reported usage, kept by its tenant from the host's Hello and
Heartbeats. `boxCapacity` comes from Hello. `boxesRunning` counts the tenant's Offered and
Running turns on the host. Placement counts the boxes a host holds from the tenant's own
sessions, never from the reported `boxesWarm`, which lags by a Heartbeat.
`channelProtocol` is the protocol version the host's latest Hello negotiated; the control plane
closes the connection with UnsupportedVersion instead of sending a frame of a newer version,
and resends it once the host reconnects on a version that speaks it. A host that has not connected since it enrolled has none.

RepositoryCloneFailureCause.description: Why the box could not clone the session's repository.

RepositoryCredentialSource.description: Where the GITHUB_TOKEN of a turn offer came from.

boxId.description: The control plane mints the id of the box that runs the turn.

goal.description: A condition the harness keeps working toward until it holds; only a session whose harness has goals in the harness catalog accepts it.

lineCount.description: How many transcript lines this turn has written so far, counting its own lines alone. A line's `lineSeq` numbers the session's lines instead, so the turn's last line is the `lineSeq` the session held before the turn plus `lineCount`.

image.description: The image the turn's box boots, recorded when the control plane offers the turn. A turn not yet offered has none.

SecretKey.description: One member of a secret set, without its value. The value never leaves the control plane in a response.

SecretMemberUpdate.description: One member of a secret set update: a new value, or none to keep the value stored under its name or its previousName.

SecretName.description: The name of a secret set member, which is also the environment variable a box gets its value in.

SecretSet.description: A named set of secrets: at most one credential per provider, and any number of variables. Values are write-only.

SecretSetCreate.description: A named set of secrets: at most one credential per provider, and any number of variables. Values are write-only.

SecretSetPatch.description:
Changes the set's name when it names one, and writes each member it lists as an update does: a
member sent without a value keeps the value stored under its previousName, or under its name when
it is not renamed. Every member it leaves out keeps its value.

SecretSetUpdate.description:
Sets the set's name and its list of members. A member the update leaves out is deleted with its
value. A member sent without a value keeps the value stored under its previousName, or under its
name when it is not renamed.

SecretValue.description: One member of a secret set with its value, written once and never read back.

value.description: The new value of the member. Left out, the member keeps the value it has stored.

previousName.description: The name the member had before this update, when the update renames it; its stored value moves with it.

repository.description: A GitHub repository as owner/name, github.com/owner/name or https://github.com/owner/name, with or without .git. A start refuses any other form and stores it as https://github.com/owner/name.

origin.description: What the session's first prompt came from: a prompt sent with Sessions_start, or the issue of Sessions_startFromIssue.

lastTurnId.description: The session's latest turn. A start offers the first turn together with the session, so every session has one.

lastTurnAt.description: When the latest turn last changed state.

lastTurn.description: The session's latest turn, with why it failed once it is Failed.

lastTurnImage.description: The image the latest turn's box boots. Present once the control plane offered the latest turn.

prebuildLayer.description:
The prebuild layer the session's files start from, or why they start without one. The control
plane records it for each box it boots while the session holds no snapshot of its own; once a
snapshot exists, every box restores that snapshot and the layer stays. Present once the control
plane offered the session's first turn.

boxRetention.description: What happens to the session's box after each turn, fixed when the session starts.

Session.description: A repository-scoped conversation with one harness and model. It outlives the boxes that run it. Its harness is its persona's, at the version the tenant pins.

turnId.description: The turn whose end left the session Idle.

SessionIssue.description: The GitHub issue of the session's repository that the session was started from, and the branch its first prompt asks for.

SessionIssueOrigin.description: The session started from a GitHub issue with Sessions_startFromIssue, with the branch its first prompt asks for.

SessionPrebuildLayerAbsent.description: The session's files start without a prebuild's layer. `detail` states why and what fixes it.

layerDigest.description: The digest the prebuild's read names for its layer.

SessionPrebuildLayerStored.description: The session's files start from a stored prebuild's layer.

SessionPromptOrigin.description: The session started with a prompt sent with Sessions_start.

repository.description: A GitHub repository as owner/name, github.com/owner/name or https://github.com/owner/name, with or without .git. A start refuses any other form and stores it as https://github.com/owner/name.

boxRetention.description: What happens to the box after each turn; left out, the session takes its persona's boxRetention.

SessionStart.description: A repository-scoped conversation with one harness and model. It outlives the boxes that run it. Its harness is its persona's, at the version the tenant pins.

Sha256Digest.description: A lower-case hex SHA-256 digest: the name of a file in the image cache, or of a persona file blob.

snapshotSeq.description: Orders a session's snapshots from 1; each one holds the whole upper directory, and a restore reads the latest.

Snapshot.description:
The overlay upper directory of a box: a SnapshotRoot under `storageKey` naming the chunks of a
SnapshotManifest that lists every entry, with the contents of its files as chunks in packs stored
under the tenant and shared by every snapshot and session of the tenant that holds the same bytes.
Exists once the host answered its request, or the snapshot deadline passed: `outcome` says
whether the root is stored or why not.

SnapshotFailure.description: The snapshot was not stored. `detail` states what failed and what fixes it.

SnapshotStored.description: The host stored the snapshot's root under its storage key. `uploadedBytes` counts the bytes that left the host: the packs the tenant held no object for, plus the root.

StartedSession.description: The answer to a start, sent before the harness writes anything.

StartedSessionFromIssue.description: The answer to a start from an issue: the start's answer and the issue the session works.

StaticConnector.description:
A remote MCP server the tenant connects once with one static token. Every session in the tenant
whose persona lists it reaches it through the box's loopback forwarder, which sends the token as
Authorization: Bearer. The URL is fixed at create; the token is write-only.

detail.description: What failed and what fixes it.

StopFailure.description: A stop that failed and returned its session to Idle with its box kept.

StopFailureReason.description: Why a stop returned its session to Idle with its box kept.

expiresAt.description: When the token stops working. A turn offered at or after it fails CredentialExpired.
When the token stops working. A turn offered at or after it fails CredentialExpired.

value.description: The new value of the member. Left out, the member keeps the value it has stored.

previousName.description: The name the member had before this update, when the update renames it; its stored value moves with it.

expiresAt.description: When the token stops working. A turn offered at or after it fails CredentialExpired.

SupervisorUpdateFailureReason.description: Why a supervisor update stopped. Every one but SupervisorUpdateRolledBack leaves the running binary in place.

SupervisorUpdateFailureReport.description:
A host's supervisor update that stopped. `detail` states what failed and what fixes it.
`outputTail` holds the last lines the candidate printed in its dry run, token-shaped runs
hidden, and is empty for every other reason.

SupervisorUpdateFailureReported.description: The latest supervisor update failure the host reported.

SupervisorUpdateNotReported.description: The host has reported no supervisor update step, or no failure, since it enrolled.

SupervisorUpdatePhase.description:
The phase a supervisor update entered. Fetching downloads and verifies the candidate binary,
DryRunning runs it with `check` beside the running binary and keeps it once it passes, Staged
is what supervisors before the box handover send while a candidate waits for the host to run no
box, Restarting swaps the binaries, parks every running turn and execs the new one, which takes
over the running boxes, and Online is the new binary reaching Welcome. WaitingForIdle is what supervisors before the idle claim send between DryRunning and
Restarting; the control plane accepts it and records nothing.

SupervisorUpdateStepReport.description:
A phase a host's supervisor update entered: from the binary `fromSha256` to `toSha256` of the
release `releaseVersion`, at `at`. `boxesRunning` counts the boxes the host ran as it entered
the phase; on Staged, the boxes the swap waits on, and on Restarting, the boxes handed over.

SupervisorUpdateStepReported.description: The latest supervisor update phase the host reported.

TenantApi.CircleCIConnectionRecord.description: The tenant's CircleCI connection as the tenant Durable Object stores it, without its secret.

expiresAtMs.description: When the OAuth token expires, in epoch milliseconds.

TenantApi.ConfigWrite.description: One write of a config apply, which the tenant Durable Object commits with the others in one transaction.

TenantApi.ConnectorStateClaims.description: The signed state of a connector authorization, as the callback reads it back.

deleted.description: False when the principal has no push subscription with the id.
False when the tenant has no webhook endpoint with the id.

TenantApi.EventCursorExpired.description: The afterEventId is older than the oldest event the log keeps.

endpoint.description: Null when the tenant has no webhook endpoint with the id.

TenantApi.GitHubUser.description: The GitHub account a repository token secret acts as, when the set holds one.

publicKey.description: The host's Ed25519 public key, base64. The private key never leaves the host.

TenantApi.HostRecord.description: A host as the control plane stores it, without its supervisor update reports.

afterEventId.description: The id after which the page starts; null starts at the current end of the log.

events.description: The event types to keep; an empty list keeps every type.

sessionId.description: The session whose events to keep; null keeps every session's.

TenantApi.NamespaceConnectionRecord.description: The tenant's Namespace connection as the tenant Durable Object stores it.

TenantApi.PatchPersonaInput.description: A persona patch, which the tenant Durable Object reads, merges and writes in one transaction, so a concurrent write never loses a field neither names.

TenantApi.PatchSecretSetInput.description: A secret set patch, which the tenant Durable Object reads, merges and writes in one transaction, so a concurrent write never loses a member neither names.

TenantApi.PersonaChange.description: What a persona edit writes. The harness is fixed at create.

TenantApi.PersonaPatchChange.description: What a persona patch writes: each field it names replaces the stored one, and every field it leaves out, and every file, stays as it is.

value.description: Null when no persona has the id.

TenantApi.PushDeliveryTarget.description: Where and how a push subscription receives its notifications.

target.description: Null when the subscription is gone.

TenantApi.RunEvent.description: A GitHub Actions workflow run event, as the webhook reports it.

TenantApi.SecretSetUnreadable.description: A stored member no longer matches its kind, so the set cannot be read.

TenantApi.StoredFile.description: A persona file as the tenant Durable Object stores it: the bytes live in the store under `digest`.

TenantApi.StoredFileRead.description: A stored persona file with its timestamps, as a persona read carries it.

TenantApi.StoredPersona.description: A persona as the tenant Durable Object stores it, its files named by digest.

boxMemoryMib.description:
The memory in MiB the box boots with: the persona's boxMemoryMib, or BoxMemoryLimit.DefaultMib. A box
that is already warm keeps the memory it booted with. A supervisor given an offer without it boots
the box with memoryMib of its runtime config.

boxDiskMib.description:
The disk in MiB the box boots with: the persona's boxDiskMib, or BoxDiskLimit.DefaultMib. A box that
is already warm keeps the disk it booted with. A supervisor given an offer without it boots the
box with overlayMib of its runtime config, and refuses the turn PoolExhausted when the disk does
not fit its disk budget.

prebuildCommitSha.description:
Set when the turn builds a prebuild: the box clones the repository at this commit and runs the
repository's setup step, /opt/tumpel/prebuild.mjs run, in place of the harness, its output lines
being the turn's lines. The credential then holds only a GITHUB_TOKEN that reads the
repository's contents, and the snapshot the control plane asks for after the turn is the
prebuild's layer.

TenantApi.StoredTurnOffer.description: A turn offer as the control plane stores it, before it adds the parts minted at each send.

TenantApi.SupervisorUpdates.description: The latest update step and failure a host reported.

TenantApi.TenantApiVersionUnsupported.description: The request names a version outside the instance's window, or an older version an adapter cannot translate. The caller answers a retryable failure.

TenantApi.TenantOperationUnknown.description: The instance does not know the operation: it runs older code. The caller answers a retryable failure.

TenantApi.TenantRefusal.description: Why the tenant Durable Object served no result.

TenantApi.TenantRequest.description: One request to the tenant Durable Object's single entry point. `operation` names the operation the way a path names a REST operation.

TenantApi.TenantRequestInvalid.description: The input fails the operation's schema: a caller bug, which the caller fails as a 500.

TenantApi.Unplaceable.description: Why placement passed over a host.

TenantApi.WriteConflict.description: A unique constraint refused the write.

TenantApiProtocol.description:
The Tenant API versions the tenant Durable Object serves, from Oldest to Version. A caller always
sends Version. Within a version only a new operation lands; every other change to an operation's
input or result raises Version, and the Durable Object keeps serving Version - 1 for one deploy.

TenantEvent.description:
A record that something happened in a tenant. The control plane appends it in the same
transaction as the state change it reports. It holds ids and the fact that changed; read the
resource for the rest.

TenantEventType.description: The kind of a tenant event, named for the state change it records.

TranscriptLine.description:
One harness-native JSONL line of a turn. `lineSeq` numbers the lines of a session from 1 and
never restarts, so a cursor stays valid across snapshots, cold boots and host moves.

Turn.description: One prompt and the harness's completion of it, run on a session's box.

detail.description: What failed and what fixes it, as the turn's failure reads.
What failed and what fixes it, with the tail of the harness's standard error when there is one.

TurnFailure.description: Why a turn ended Failed. Exists only for a turn in state Failed.

TurnFailureReason.description: Why a turn ended Failed. Each reason names the phase the turn stopped in.

TurnFullImage.description: The turn's box boots a full guest image. `guestImageDigest` names the same image as a prebuild's guestImageDigest.

TurnImage.description: The image a turn's box boots.

TurnLayeredImage.description: The turn's box boots a base image with the harness layer of the session's harness version.

goal.description: A condition the harness keeps working toward until it holds; only a session whose harness has goals in the harness catalog accepts it.

TurnSend.description: The fields every turn carries, whatever its state.

WebhookDeliveryStatus.description: Whether a webhook endpoint receives its events, with how it fails when it does not.

WebhookEndpoint.description:
An HTTPS endpoint that receives the tenant's events of the listed types, in eventId order, at
least once. Each request is a POST of one event as JSON. Its `Tumpel-Signature` header is the
base64url Ed25519 signature, under the tenant's webhook signing key, over the request body;
`Tumpel-Event-Id` repeats the eventId so a receiver drops a repeat. A failed request is retried
after 1 minute, doubling to 1 hour. The URL and types are fixed at create.

WebhookEndpointCreate.description:
An HTTPS endpoint that receives the tenant's events of the listed types, in eventId order, at
least once. Each request is a POST of one event as JSON. Its `Tumpel-Signature` header is the
base64url Ed25519 signature, under the tenant's webhook signing key, over the request body;
`Tumpel-Event-Id` repeats the eventId so a receiver drops a repeat. A failed request is retried
after 1 minute, doubling to 1 hour. The URL and types are fixed at create.

detail.description: How the last request failed: the status the endpoint answered, or that it did not answer within 10 seconds.

WebhookUrl.description:
The HTTPS address a webhook endpoint receives events at. It carries no user info and no
fragment, so it never holds a credential.

WorkflowPath.description: A workflow file of the tenant's repositories, such as .github/workflows/tumpel-prebuild.yml.
